newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens bourse president rushes home to face row.
newsitem.headline: Athens bourse president rushes home to face row.

text.p: Athens bourse president Manolis Xanthakis headed home early from a trip to Asia after Greek brokerages halted all trade with a boycott, saying the clearing house had failed to pay some members, his office said on Friday.
Xanthakis was cutting his trip short by a day to rush home from a conference in Hong Kong on European stock exchanges, a secretary in his office told reporters.
Brokerage bosses decided to boycott trade, effectively closing the bourse, after saying the clearing house had failed to pay several firms on Thursday.
The boycott was aimed at putting pressure on the government to intervene before the issue spun out of control, brokers said.

"Instead of intervening fast to cover the cash problem which is of a relatively small magnitude and allow the system to keep on going, the government is being indecisive. This could grow into a big problem," said one brokerage boss, who requested anonymity.
No explanation has been given by the clearing house for its failure to pay some of the brokerages.
